2027-04-23.title: Fourth Friday of Resurrection
2027-04-23.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-04-23.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta). In the Latin calendar today is St George, martyr; the Syro-Malabar calendar keeps the feast of St George (Geevarghese Sahada) tomorrow, 24 April (verify locally). Even in the Easter season every Friday recalls the Lord's Passion; follow your eparchy's norms on Friday penance.
2027-04-23.verse: Therefore it says, “Sleeper, awake! Rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.”
theo: In the middle of a page of practical advice, Paul suddenly quotes a few lines that sound like a song: “Sleeper, awake! Rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.” Many scholars think this was a hymn sung at Baptism in the first Christian communities. One can imagine the newly baptised coming up from the water while the community sang it over them. The words gather the whole of Easter into three short lines: we were asleep, we were dead, and Christ, the Sun risen from the tomb, has shone on us. Paul has just said that “everything exposed by the light becomes visible”. The light of Christ does not only warm us; it shows us the truth about ourselves, and what is brought into his light is healed. That is why the Church has always loved to call Baptism illumination. In the Easter season the paschal candle stands near the altar in some of our churches, and the newly baptised receive a lit candle: they are sleepers who have been woken and dead who have risen.

Then Paul draws the consequences for daily life. “Be careful then how you live, not as unwise people but as wise, making the most of the time, because the days are evil.” The Christian is awake, and an awake person does not waste the day. He warns against drunkenness, which dulls the mind and wrecks families, and offers another kind of fullness instead: “be filled with the Spirit, as you sing psalms and hymns and spiritual songs among yourselves, singing and making melody to the Lord in your hearts, giving thanks to God the Father at all times and for everything in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.” The Spirit-filled Church is a singing and thankful Church. Our Syro-Malabar tradition knows this well: the Qurbana is sung, the hours of prayer are sung, and the homes of our grandparents rang each evening with the family prayer and its songs. Paul ends with a word that opens the next section on family life: “Be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ.” Mutual service is the fruit of the Spirit; a home where each gives way to the other for Christ's sake is already full of his light.

The Gospel is Mark's account of the feeding of the five thousand. It is late, the place is deserted, and the disciples want to send the crowd away to buy food. Jesus answers: “You give them something to eat.” They protest that two hundred denarii would hardly be enough. “How many loaves have you? Go and see.” Five, and two fish. Then Mark describes what Jesus does with words every Christian recognises: “Taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven, and blessed and broke the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before the people.” Took, blessed, broke, gave: these are the very actions of the Last Supper and of every Qurbana. All ate and were filled, and twelve baskets of fragments were left over, one for each apostle, as if to say that the Church will never run out of this bread. Two lessons stand out for this Easter Friday. First, Jesus works through the disciples: he does not drop bread from the sky but asks them to bring what little they have and to hand it out. Second, he feeds the people with abundance: the Risen Lord still gives himself in the Eucharist to all who come, and he still says to his Church in the face of every hunger, of body and of soul, “You give them something to eat.”
conn: “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you” (Isaiah 60:1).
“For once you were darkness, but now in the Lord you are light. Live as children of light” (Ephesians 5:8).
“O sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth” (Psalm 96:1); “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly… sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs to God” (Colossians 3:16).
“They shall eat and have some left” (2 Kings 4:43–44): twenty barley loaves for a hundred people.
John's account adds that the five barley loaves and two fish belonged to a boy (John 6:9).
The same four actions at the Last Supper (Mark 14:22) and at Emmaus, where the disciples knew him “in the breaking of the bread” (Luke 24:30–35).
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Lord does again what he did in the deserted place: he takes the bread, gives thanks, breaks it and gives it through his ministers, and the bread is now his own Body, the true Bread from heaven.
Our small offerings brought to the altar are like the five loaves: little in our hands, abundant in his.
outline: Point 1 · Christ will shine on you
Baptism as illumination, and the light that heals.
Point 2 · Be filled with the Spirit
Wise living, singing and thanksgiving at all times.
Point 3 · You give them something to eat
Five loaves, four actions and twelve baskets.
A parish kitchen on a Friday evening where a few volunteers feed many.
“Sleeper, awake! Rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.”
live: Begin tomorrow with a short prayer of light: Christ, shine on me today.
Sing one hymn together as a family at evening prayer this week.
Before sleep tonight, name three things you are thankful for, including one that was hard.
Offer one small skill or a little money to a parish or charity that feeds the hungry.
fathers: The Lord says, Awake, you who sleep, and rise from the dead, and Christ the Lord will shine on you: the Sun of the Resurrection, begotten before the morning star, who gives life by his own rays. Let us open our eyes to that light and walk in the day.
In your Bread is hidden the Spirit who cannot be consumed; in your Wine dwells the Fire that cannot be drunk. The Spirit in your Bread, the Fire in your Wine: a wonder that our lips receive.
magis: Baptism is called enlightenment, because those who receive it are enlightened in their understanding; having received the Word, the true light, the baptised person becomes a son of light.

The miracles of the multiplication of the loaves, when the Lord said the blessing, broke and distributed the loaves through his disciples to feed the multitude, prefigure the superabundance of this unique bread of his Eucharist.
Thanksgiving characterises the prayer of the Church; every event and need can become an offering of thanksgiving.
Song and music are closely linked to the liturgy; singing with the heart is a sign of the Church's prayer.
God blesses those who come to the aid of the poor; love for the poor is part of the Church's constant tradition.
saints: Latin calendar: St George, martyr. In the Syro-Malabar calendar his feast falls tomorrow, Saturday 24 April.

19–25 April: fourth week of the Resurrection. Wed 21: in the Latin calendar, St Anselm. Fri 23: in the Latin calendar, St George. Sat 24: in the Syro-Malabar calendar, St George, Martyr (Geevarghese Sahada), an important feast. Sun 25: Fifth Sunday of Resurrection, with Mar Addai; St Mark the Evangelist (25 Apr) gives way to the Sunday this year (verify locally).
2027-04-23.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Sun of the Resurrection, you woke us from sleep and raised us from death in Baptism; shine on us today. Fill us with your Holy Spirit, so that we may live wisely, sing your praises and give thanks to the Father at all times and for everything. As you fed the hungry crowd in the deserted place, feed us with the Bread of your Body, and make us generous to all who hunger. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen. Alleluia!

2027-04-23.action: Give thanks before every meal today, slowly, as Jesus did.
2027-04-23.question: What small loaves do I have that Jesus could use to feed someone?
kidsaint: Mother Teresa saw poor people dying alone on the streets of Kolkata. She began with almost nothing: a few rupees and a few helpers. She said she was doing small things with great love. Soon her sisters were feeding and caring for thousands of people in many countries. Lesson: give Jesus your little loaves, and he will feed many!
2027-04-23.special: Fourth Friday of Resurrection. Latin calendar: St George.
term: An ancient name for Baptism (in Greek photismos), used by Justin Martyr and the Fathers. The newly baptised were called the enlightened, because Christ the light had shone on them; this is why a lit candle is given at Baptism.

family.explain: A huge crowd was hungry in a place with no shops. The disciples had only five loaves and two fish. Jesus took them, looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke them and gave them to the disciples to share. Everyone ate until they were full, and there were twelve baskets left over! Jesus does something even more wonderful at the Holy Qurbana: he gives us himself as the Bread of life.
family.intention: We pray for children who are hungry today, and for all who feed them.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we share this week with someone who does not have enough?”

illus: A parish in Thrissur began a Friday evening meal for migrant workers and lonely elderly people. On the first evening the volunteers had cooked for forty, and more than seventy came. The young assistant priest stood in the kitchen wondering what to do. An old woman who helped every week said, “Father, do what Jesus did. Say the blessing and start serving.” They served smaller portions, and somehow everyone ate. When the last plate was cleared, there was still rice in the pot. The priest said later that he had read the story of the loaves many times, but that night he understood the line, “You give them something to eat.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Sun of the Resurrection, shine on us now. Fill us with your Spirit, and teach us to give thanks for everything. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Sleeper, awake! Rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you (Ephesians 5:14). Where am I spiritually asleep?
Making the most of the time, because the days are evil (Ephesians 5:16). How do I use my time each day?
Giving thanks to God the Father at all times and for everything (Ephesians 5:20). What am I slow to thank God for?
You give them something to eat (Mark 6:37). Whom is Jesus asking me to feed?
pm.resp: Christ, shine on us and fill us.
interc: For the newly baptised, that the light of Christ may shine in their lives.
For families broken by alcohol and addiction, that they may find healing and the fullness of the Spirit.
For the hungry and for migrant workers far from home, that they may find bread and welcome.
For parish volunteers and all who feed the poor, that the Lord may multiply their gifts.
For ourselves, that we may receive the Holy Qurbana with thanksgiving and share what we have.
pm.close: Father, your Son took the loaves, blessed, broke and gave them, and fed the multitude. Feed us with the Bread of life, fill us with your Spirit, and make us wise, thankful and generous. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, today Paul gives us a little hymn, and Mark gives us the feeding of the five thousand.

The hymn says: “Sleeper, awake! Rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.” The first Christians probably sang it at Baptism. We were asleep, we were dead, and the Risen Christ has shone on us. That is why Baptism is called illumination, and why we receive a lit candle.

Then Paul says: be careful how you live; make the most of the time; do not get drunk, but be filled with the Spirit, singing psalms and hymns and “giving thanks to God the Father at all times and for everything.” A Spirit-filled home is a singing and thankful home.

In the Gospel, the crowd is hungry and the place is deserted. Jesus says to the disciples: “You give them something to eat.” They have only five loaves and two fish. He takes them, blesses, breaks and gives them through the disciples, and all are filled, with twelve baskets left over.
These are the actions of every Holy Qurbana. The Risen Lord still feeds his people with his own Body, and he still asks us to bring our small loaves and to share them with the hungry.
So today, let us wake up to Christ's light, give thanks for everything, and bring our little gifts to him. He will make them enough. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus fed five thousand people with five loaves and two fish! He took the bread, said thank you to God, broke it and shared it.
At the Holy Qurbana Jesus gives us the best bread of all: himself. Today, share something with a friend, like Jesus did!

points.h: You give them something to eat
q: So he repeated, “Give it to the people and let them eat, for thus says the LORD, ‘They shall eat and have some left.’”
Taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven, and blessed and broke the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before the people; and he divided the two fish among them all.
points.apply: Offer a skill, some time or a little money to those who feed the hungry.

concl: The Risen Christ shines on us, fills us with his Spirit and feeds us with his Body.
Let us wake, give thanks and bring our small loaves to him.
2027-04-23.resolve: This week, pray each morning for Christ's light, give thanks before every meal, and share bread with someone who is hungry.
